context_candidates.text:
Poverty reduction is especially difficult in economies affected by conflict and institutional weakness, which typically face compounding challenges even after the conflict has subsided (Corral et al. 2020; Federle et al. 2024; Korn and Stemmler 2025; Novta and Pugacheva 2021; World Bank 2025b). Conflict destroys assets and disrupts livelihoods, whereas poverty fuels grievances and weakens the capacity of the state to prevent violence (Corral et al. 2020).

These challenges are compounded by the current global environment, in which economies dependent on energy imports and economies directly affected by conflict face the weakest growth prospects (World Bank 2026c). Furthermore, when a population grows quickly, the economy must expand even more quickly to deliver the same level of improvement in per capita welfare.
